evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, numbers and figure briefs are original.

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use Lesson 2: q01 direct retrieval and q07 mixed application.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: retrieval and graph diagnosis to gradient calculation, limit identification and multi-step comparison

questions.prompt: A spring extends 18.0 mm under a force of 4.50 N while proportional behaviour continues. Calculate its spring constant.
State two graph features that show force is proportional to extension.
A force-extension graph is straight but does not pass through the origin. Which statement is correct?

options.C: The relation is linear but not proportional.

questions.prompt: Two force-extension lines pass through the origin. Line P is steeper than line Q. What can be concluded?

options.A: P has a larger spring constant and is stiffer.
options.B: P has a smaller spring constant and is stiffer.
options.C: Q has a larger spring constant and is stiffer.
options.D: Both have the same spring constant.

questions.prompt: A force-extension graph is initially straight, then begins to curve. Which point represents the limit of proportionality?

options.B: The point where the graph first departs from the initial straight trend
options.C: The midpoint of the straight section

questions.prompt: A force-extension graph has a straight section through the origin. Two points on its best-fit line are (8.0 mm, 1.6 N) and (32.0 mm, 6.4 N). Calculate the gradient in N m⁻¹ and explain its physical meaning. The graph first departs from the straight trend at 7.2 N. State the limit of proportionality and explain why a single spring constant should not be calculated using a point well beyond it.

figure.purpose: Assess gradient selection and limit interpretation
figure.brief: Original black-and-white force-extension axes with a straight line through the origin that curves after 7.2 N. Mark only the two stated coordinate points; do not mark a gradient triangle or label the limit.
figure.alt_text: A force-extension graph is straight through two marked points and then curves after a force of 7.2 newtons.

questions.prompt: Springs A and B have straight force-extension graphs through the origin. At 6.0 N, A extends 24 mm and B extends 15 mm. Calculate the spring constant of each spring and identify the stiffer spring. Spring A begins to leave its straight trend at 7.5 N. Predict its extension at 7.5 N, then explain why using the same calculation to predict its extension at 10.0 N is unsafe.

figure.purpose: Assess comparison of stiffness and conditional prediction at a graph boundary
figure.brief: Original black-and-white paired force-extension graph with straight lines A and B through the origin, the given 6.0 N coordinates, and A beginning to curve at 7.5 N. Omit gradients, stiffness labels and predicted extensions.
figure.alt_text: Two force-extension graphs show different slopes, and spring A begins to curve at 7.5 newtons.
